_comment: The navigation policy every native shell with its own code implements, as test vectors.
Two implementations answer 'may this shell show this URL?': the Android home launcher
(OriginPolicy.kt, JVM unit test) and the desktop shell (policy.js, test/native.mjs). They
are deliberately NOT one shared implementation — they run in different languages on
different platforms — so they are held to one DECLARED behaviour instead: both must
return `allow` for every case below, or their own test fails.
The rule: https only, no userinfo, the default port only, and the origin (scheme + host,
case-insensitive) exactly equal to a listed origin. No suffix, prefix or pattern match.
Inputs are what a real engine hands the policy: a canonical URL (Chromium has already
normalised it) or something plainly not a web URL. Parser-disagreement inputs (a
backslash in the authority) are left out on purpose — Chromium never emits them, and the
two parsers may legitimately differ on them as long as neither allows a foreign host.

cases.why: a listed origin
no path at all
path, query and fragment are not the origin
the sign-in hop; a query naming another host changes nothing
scheme and host compare case-insensitively
an explicit default port is the default port
cleartext: the right host over the wrong scheme
a non-default port is a different origin
a sibling subdomain that is not listed
a listed origin as a PREFIX of a foreign host
a listed host as a SUFFIX of a foreign host
a listed origin inside the query
a listed origin inside the fragment
userinfo: the host is evil.example
any userinfo at all, even on a listed host
a trailing-dot FQDN is not the listed origin string
script URL
local file
Android content provider
Android intent URL
data URL
a blob URL is not a navigation to its origin
not a web origin
garbage fails closed
empty fails closed
